title: Compliance Bulletin: The State Basis of Late Charges on Auto Loans
content:
## 1. The state that governs

1.1 The late charge on a loan of the Auto Loans line follows the borrower's state of residence as the customer profile shows it on the installment's due date.

## 2. When a charge arises

2.1 A late charge applies to an installment not satisfied within the grace days that state publishes, counted in calendar days after the installment's due date.

2.2 Calendar days are counted with the day after the installment's due date as day 1. The charge applies when the present date is after the installment's due date plus that state's grace days and the installment is still unsatisfied at the end of that last grace day.

2.3 The charge is recorded against the installment that was late and is dated the first day after the grace days end.

## 3. Withdrawn basis

3.1 The basis by which the amount of a late charge was worked out is **no longer in force**.

## 4. Limits on when a charge may arise at all

4.1 Each installment carries at most one late charge.

4.2 No late charge applies to an installment deferred by a payment extension, to the part of a payment that went to charges, or to a loan that has been charged off or paid off.

## 5. Where the charge sits afterwards

5.1 Late charges are recorded among the unpaid charges on the loan and are paid first out of later payments.

## 6. Boundary illustration

6.1 For a borrower whose state publishes 15 grace days: on the fifteenth day counted from the day after the due date, the grace days have not yet run out and no charge arises even where the installment is unsatisfied. On the sixteenth day, the grace days have run out; where the installment was still unsatisfied at the end of the fifteenth day, the charge arises and is dated that sixteenth day.

6.2 For a borrower whose state publishes 7 grace days, the same reading falls on the seventh and the eighth day.

## 7. A point of judgement on the state test

7.1 The state that governs is the state on the profile on the installment's due date, not the state on the day the question is asked. A borrower who moved from Virginia to North Carolina after an installment fell due is judged on the state their profile showed on that due date.

superseded_clauses: The charge equals late_charge_pct_by_state percent of monthly_payment, rounded half-up to the cent, capped at late_charge_cap_by_state
